problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a wastewater purification strategy to lower total nitrogen discharge from several industrial effluent outlets. Initially, no treatment technologies have been implemented.

The profile of each discharge outlet is as follows:
* For Outlet 1, discharge coefficient is 1.295, flow volume is 103.338.
* For Outlet 2, discharge coefficient is 1.05, flow volume is 132.971.
* For Outlet 3, discharge coefficient is 0.96, flow volume is 140.199.
* For Outlet 4, discharge coefficient is 0.67, flow volume is 104.611.
* For Outlet 5, discharge coefficient is 1.763, flow volume is 238.164.
* For Outlet 6, discharge coefficient is 1.54, flow volume is 182.625.
* For Outlet 7, discharge coefficient is 1.843, flow volume is 299.158.
* For Outlet 8, discharge coefficient is 0.73, flow volume is 255.922.
* For Outlet 9, discharge coefficient is 1.053, flow volume is 295.283.

To abate discharges, multiple purification technologies are accessible, each defined by a specific removal rate:
* Technology1 eliminates 89% of pollutants.
* Technology2 eliminates 36% of pollutants.
* Technology3 eliminates 54% of pollutants.
* Technology4 eliminates 18% of pollutants.
* Technology5 eliminates 41% of pollutants.
* Technology6 eliminates 40% of pollutants.
* Technology7 eliminates 13% of pollutants.
* Technology8 eliminates 35% of pollutants.
* Technology9 eliminates 64% of pollutants.

Deploying a technology at an outlet induces an incremental expense per unit of flow volume. The expense matrix for all outlet–technology pairings is provided below:

| Outlet \ Technology | Technology1 | Technology2 | Technology3 | Technology4 | Technology5 | Technology6 | Technology7 | Technology8 | Technology9 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Outlet 1 | 184.027 | 189.548 | 83.316 | 112.645 | 63.738 | 183.154 | 166.201 | 81.242 | 162.535 |
| Outlet 2 | 94.656 | 18.332 | 180.674 | 46.577 | 107.64 | 190.16 | 41.805 | 191.692 | 112.215 |
| Outlet 3 | 11.393 | 22.44 | 137.364 | 156.981 | 174.341 | 90.6 | 29.746 | 112.173 | 143.521 |
| Outlet 4 | 195.483 | 157.289 | 132.847 | 188.553 | 151.909 | 39.213 | 97.253 | 73.026 | 26.629 |
| Outlet 5 | 20.311 | 160.901 | 116.036 | 119.243 | 53.253 | 59.143 | 83.726 | 129.741 | 92.275 |
| Outlet 6 | 13.209 | 137.927 | 111.619 | 131.87 | 127.486 | 153.633 | 121.266 | 143.168 | 23.792 |
| Outlet 7 | 186.329 | 30.166 | 159.509 | 67.257 | 26.436 | 155.402 | 93.158 | 85.072 | 135.537 |
| Outlet 8 | 100.058 | 111.359 | 35.912 | 84.289 | 161.522 | 113.688 | 192.426 | 37.374 | 138.685 |
| Outlet 9 | 183.692 | 161.053 | 148.572 | 80.895 | 190.398 | 115.17 | 115.463 | 33.415 | 10.956 |

Determine how to assign purification technologies to each outlet (outlets may employ multiple technologies concurrently), and observe that an outlet may also remain partially untreated if required.
The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate nitrogen discharge is diminished by at least a proportion P = 0.498 of the baseline load, while minimizing the total expenditure.
